hypothese.summary: Multi-house luxury group (Gucci, Saint Laurent, Bottega Veneta, Balenciaga, McQueen, Brioni, Boucheron/Pomellato/Qeelin jewellery, Kering Eyewear) emerging from a severe 2023-2025 crisis (revenue -27% and ROI -71% between 2022 and 2025, with 2025 marked by a net loss on a continuing basis): H1 2026 marks a tangible inflection - return to growth in Q2 (first positive quarter after 12 quarters of decline), margin in clear expansion (+300bp vs H2 2025) and massive deleveraging (-4,7 Md€ in H1, driven by the Kering Beauté/real estate disposals), but Gucci remains in comparable decline (-2% in Q2) and China requires multi-year groundwork. Thesis of gradual rebuilding, not a rapid return to historical margins (30% in 2019).
hypothese.text:
== THESIS SUMMARY ==
Kering is a multi-house luxury turnaround indexed on Gucci (~40% of sales). The 2022-2025 cycle was a disaster - group sales down 28% to EUR 14.7bn, recurring operating income down 71% to EUR 1.63bn (margin 27.5% -> 11.1%), published 2025 net collapsing to EUR 72M - driven by Gucci's desirability crisis (sales halved to ~EUR 6bn) and a structurally weaker China. The thesis is the Luca de Meo reset (CEO since 2025, Capital Markets Day April 2026): Rinascimento at Gucci, 250 net store closures 2026-2030, EUR 1bn inventory reduction, group platform mutualization - a PROGRESSIVE rebuild toward an ~18% margin by 2030, deliberately far below the historical 27-30% peak. S1 2026 delivered the first tangible proof: +2% comparable in Q2 (first growth in 12 quarters), Gucci improving sequentially (-2% Q2 vs -8% Q1), group margin 12.8% (+300bp vs S2 2025), and net debt HALVED in six months to EUR 3.3bn (Kering Beaute sold to L'Oreal for EUR 4bn, Milan real estate disposal) - the market repriced +15.9% on the day. The path stays non-linear by management's own words: Q3 guided 'probably flat', China needs multi-year fundamental work, no buybacks in 2026.

== THESIS READ ==
- First comparable-growth quarter in 12 (+2% Q2) with margin inflection (12.8% S1, +300bp vs S2 25): the reset is delivering earlier than the prudent trajectory assumed.
- Deleveraging is effectively done as a risk factor: net debt 8.0 -> 3.3bn EUR in six months (1.4x EBITDA), financial charges falling fast (-26% S1) - the bridge now carries 500 -> 150M EUR of declining finNet through 2030.
- Gucci not yet fixed: still -5% comparable S1; the Demna Primavera collection (in stores since mid-July, major campaign late August) is the key S2 test.
- Store rationalization ahead of plan (84 net closures S1 vs 100 targeted FY) and OpEx guidance improved to 'down' - cost side over-delivers while the top line heals.
- Watch: Q3 guided 'probably flat' on tough comps - a positive surprise there would de-risk the 2027 re-acceleration assumption.

== SPECIAL FACTORS ==
None.

== PARAMETERS & WATCH-LIST ==
Base: Kering's published recurring operating income (clean by construction - the company itself excludes non-recurring items). d-bis APPLIED at this refresh: data.2025.net now carries the company's recurring net income (EUR 532M); the published GAAP figure (EUR 72M: recurring 532 - net non-recurring charges to -29 continuing + ~101 disposal gain in discontinued) is traced here and in the bridge residual - the CAGR engine no longer starts from a noise floor. Bridge (c-ter): the prior thesis parameters reconcile EXACTLY (tax 31% 2026 -> 27.5% from 2028 per management's gradual-normalization guidance; finNet 500 -> 150M EUR with deleveraging); 2025's 'other' -248M recurring non-op drag to split at a future refresh. Projections unchanged. Scorecard: directional-guidance house - FY26 anchor posed on the imperfect mid-year consensus (6.48, 23/06, pre-beat; re-anchor Feb 2027), history not measurable, application suspended (turnaround regime). Semiannual EPS split deferred: S1 recurring net not captured from sources this refresh - build at next refresh from the interim report, with the GAAP/IFRS statements pass (etatsFinanciers queue). WATCH-LIST: (1) Q3 (29/10) vs the 'flattish' guide; (2) Primavera sell-through; (3) dedicated China plan first checkpoint (November); (4) EUR 1bn inventory target by year-end; (5) Gucci Beauty license shift to L'Oreal (royalty model from mid-2027, unquantified); (6) post-results consensus refresh (current anchor stale).

== CATALYSTS ==
Q3 sales (29 Oct): first test of the 'flattish' guide and Primavera reception; late-August Gucci campaign; China plan checkpoint in November; financial charges melting with the deleveraging.

ancrages.moteur: Qualitative official guidance only (no precise figures): revenue growth in 2026 vs 2025 confirmed at H1. Rebuilt bottom-up: actual H1 2026 (7 220 M€) + H2 2026 estimated at ~7 580 M€ (Q3 comparable 'flattish' as guided by management with a close-to-neutral FX effect, Q4 in moderate acceleration driven by Primavera/Core Cruise on an already less demanding Q4 2025 comparison base) - taken prudently below the pace of Q2 alone (+2% comparable) given management's explicit warning of a flattish Q3.

Continuation of a gradual rebuilding of revenue at +5%/yr over 2027-2029 then +5,5% in 2030, driven by the expected stabilisation of Gucci, the continued strong momentum of Kering Jewelry (+20% comparable in H1 2026) and Kering Eyewear (+8%), and the lapping of the difficult FX/comparison effects of 2025-2026 - linear rebuilding assumption for want of quantified guidance beyond 2026, at low confidence by construction.

Official guidance: H2 2026 margin above the H1 margin (12,8%). Taken at ~14,5% in H2 (continued cost discipline, Q4 volume operating leverage mentioned by management), giving a consolidated FY2026 margin of 13,6% (vs 11,1% in FY2025) - bottom-up rebuild from actual H1 + estimated H2, consistent with the 190-220bp of annual margin expansion mentioned by management on H1 alone.

Continuation of a gradual expansion of the recurring operating margin towards 15,0% (2027), 16,3% (2028), 17,3% (2029) and 18,0% (2030) - a prudent rebuilding trajectory deliberately well below the group's historical peaks (24,3% in 2023, 27,5% in 2022, 30,1% in 2019), reflecting the absence of quantified medium-term guidance and a thesis of measured recovery rather than a rapid return to pre-crisis margins.

Net financial charges projected to fall rapidly, consistently with the deleveraging already achieved (net debt divided by more than 2 in H1 2026, cost of net debt in H1 2026 down 26% vs H1 2025): taken at 500 M€ in FY2026 (vs 594 M€ in FY2025), then 380/280/200/150 M€ over 2027-2030 as net debt tends towards zero.
Normative tax rate aligned with management's EXPLICIT guidance (gradual return towards the normative 27-28% range over 2 to 3 years, from 32,5% in H1 2026): 31% (2026), 29% (2027), 27,5% (2028-2030).

Continued deleveraging at a rapid pace driven by free cash flow generation (1,8 Md€ in H1 2026 excluding exceptional items, +68% vs H1 2025) in the absence of any new major disposal identified and of any buyback programme: net debt projected at ~2,5 Md€ at end-2026 (vs 3,3 Md€ at 30/06/2026), then a continued decline towards a position close to neutrality in 2030.

Diluted share count held stable at ~122,6M across the whole horizon - no buyback programme planned in 2026 according to management (priority to deleveraging and to investment in the houses), historical dilution close to nil.

No direct EPS-vs-consensus comparison exists for the S1 26 publication (recurring operating metrics only were benchmarked by same-day coverage); epsAdj.basis set to null - the prior free-text explanation moved here from the basis field (C16).

dernierCall.guidanceProchainTrimestre: No quantified quarterly guidance. Clear qualitative signal, repeated three times in Q&A (de Meo, then confirmed to Barclays and UBS): Q3 2026 seen 'probably flat' in GROUP comparable terms - tougher year-on-year comps, product newness concentrated late in the year and a still-volatile macro - with Q4 expected to improve on the full Primavera rollout (stores since 15 July, major marketing campaign late August) plus the Core Cruise collection launch; wholesale roughly flat in H2. Management framed the path as non-linear while recommitting to the full-year outcome.
dernierCall.guidanceAnnuelle: FY26 qualitative guidance reconfirmed by the CEO at the close of the presentation: growth and improved profitability vs 2025 (no figures). Firmed up on three fronts during the call: (1) H2 recurring margin explicitly guided ABOVE H1's 12.8% (CFO, confirmed twice in Q&A); (2) full-year OpEx now guided DOWN (vs 'flat' guided early 2026; -5% reported / -3% cc in H1), no quantification; (3) at least 100 net store closures in 2026 confirmed (84 done in H1) with the COO signalling the 250-by-2030 CMD plan can run faster (~similar pace possible in 2027). EUR 1bn F&LG inventory-reduction target (Sept 2025-Dec 2026) confirmed on track. Further H2 net-debt reduction from operating cash flow alone; no share buyback in 2026; M&A restricted to selective bolt-ons; tax rate to return gradually to the 27-28% normative range over 2-3 years (32.5% in H1).
pointsCles: Inflection confirmed: +2% comparable in Q2 2026, the first positive quarter after 12 consecutive quarters of decline (Q1 flat), achieved WHILE closing 84 net stores in H1 (on top of 75 in 2025) - CEO Luca de Meo called it an important milestone but stressed the recovery will be non-linear, guiding Q3 'probably flat' for the group on tougher comps and a volatile macro.

Gucci sharply better sequentially but not yet fixed: -2% comparable in Q2 vs -8% in Q1 (+6pts, retail improving in ALL regions), H1 sales EUR 2.8bn (-5%), margin 17% (+1pt); leather goods back to growth (Borsetto, Paparazzo) and the top 100-120 'retail excellence lab' stores responding well - but management declined to endorse the analyst consensus (Morgan Stanley question) of a positive Q3, pinning the real test on Demna's first complete collection Primavera (in stores since 15 July, major campaign late August).

Margin and cost delivery ahead of plan: H1 recurring operating margin 12.8% (+40bp YoY, +300bp vs H2 2025) on OpEx down 5% (-3% cc) with A&P held at ~9% of sales; OpEx now guided DOWN for FY26 (vs flat initially), H2 margin explicitly guided above H1's 12.8%, and the EUR 1bn F&LG inventory-reduction target (Sept 2025-Dec 2026) confirmed well on track with deliberate, sizeable production cuts - full-price sales robust, no discount-driven quarter per the COO.

Balance-sheet risk essentially extinguished: net debt halved to EUR 3.3bn (-4.7bn in six months; 1.4x adjusted EBITDA) on the EUR 4bn Kering Beaute/Creed disposal to L'Oreal and real-estate sales (EUR 700M Via Monte Napoleone), FCF ex-disposals EUR 1.8bn (+68%), cost of net debt -26%; further H2 deleveraging to come from operating cash flow alone, no buyback in 2026, and the new 50-year Gucci Beauty licence to L'Oreal (7 July, one year early, after the ~USD 400M Coty exit) reshapes the beauty model from mid-2027.
